text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed an oscillation in cross-region routing during the EU maintenance window (10:25-10:40). Latency-based steering bumped US weights but a big chunk of client traffic remained pinned to eu-lb. Also seeing NAT port saturation on eu-egress. Anyone else seeing this?

mija: Saw it too. GeoDNS returned updated weights but ALB session affinity + failing health probes kept traffic on EU. Brief log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T10:29:12Z eu-lb-1 healthcheck timeout 504
2026-03-18T10:29:20Z eu-lb-1 conn_count spike -> 18k
2026-03-18T10:30:05Z iptables: SNAT ports exhausted for 10.2.5.0/24
```

sanjay: We rolled the weighted routing change (traffic-weight-rollout v2) at 10:28, bumped us weight 0.1->0.5. Deploy-bot shows a rollback at 10:34. My suspicion: long-lived connections + LB affinity prevented client rebalancing, so new connections hit US but old sessions stayed pinned to EU.

claire: NAT port exhaustion makes it worse — sockets sticking to old backend keep EU hot while new sessions fail creating a feedback loop. For eu-nodepool-gpu we have limited ephemeral ports per node. Short-term: expand SNAT pool or add more SNAT IPs. Medium-term: move to per-pod egress or keepalive/conn-drain improvements.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Reverted geo-weight-rollout v2 at 2026-03-18T10:34:12. ChangeID: ch_789. Rollback reason: client 5xx spike in EU region.

opsbot: opsbot: Alert -> EU SNAT usage > 92% (nodepool-gpu-eu-1) for 6m. Autoscale attempted, hit quota error. Ticket created: INC-4021.

alex: Immediate remediation plan proposal:
1) Hotfix: increase egress SNAT ports/IPs in EU by +50% (limit risk: we need to check quota).
2) Health probes: change threshold from 1 failure -> 2 consecutive failures to reduce probe jitter induced flips.
3) GeoDNS TTL: shorten from 300s -> 60s (let clients rebalance faster).
4) Routing policy tweak: add a fallback_weight_floor = 0.15 so no region can drop to 0 during rollouts.
Thoughts? :thinking_face:

mija: +1 on SNAT expansion and probe tweak. For TTL I'm leaning to 60s not 30s to avoid too much churn. Also suggest we add a 'grace window' for weighted rollouts so we don't ramp weights until probes are stable for X seconds.

sanjay: I'll draft a rollout policy: hold new weights in pending for 120s, require health OK for 90s, then ramp 25% every 60s. Auto-rollback if error rate > 2% for 5m. Also implementing fallback_weight_floor as suggested.

claire: Quick cost note: shifting 40% traffic => US on-demand GPU usage up ~18% during peak (estimates from last month). We should add a finance-aware knob in the routing decision (cost_bias) so we can prefer cheaper regions when performance delta is small.

alex: Good call. For immediate hotfix: can we do SNAT IP add + probe threshold change now? I'll schedule 2hr window for full weight-retry rollout after hotfix.

mija: I'll open RFC + infra task. Hotfix plan: patch iptables SNAT on eu-nodes and update LB probe config. Trying the SNAT IP add now, will update in 15m.

sanjay: I'll open the PR for rollout policy. Will include: YAML schema and a simulation harness to test oscillation.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: ch_790 scheduled: iptables-snat-increase on eu-nodepool at 11:05 UTC. ETA ~10m.

opsbot: opsbot: Auto-escalation sent to oncall and infra. Monitoring dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/EGRESS/eu-snat-usage and Prometheus queries: `sum(node_snat_used_ports) by (nodepool)`

alex: After hotfix we should run a synthetic ttfb/latency experiment to verify clients actually shift. If not, next steps: disable LB affinity for new connections and drain sessions, or enable region-level connection draining.

mija: Agreed. I'll also add a small runbook: steps to bump SNAT, revert DNS TTL change, and emergency circuit-breaker to pin traffic by account if needed.

sanjay: Drafted rollout policy snippet (for RFC) — will paste into RFC but here for quick reference:
```
rollout_policy:
  kind: weighted-failover
  grace_window_seconds: 120
  ramp_step_percent: 25
  health_ok_seconds: 90
  fallback_weight_floor: 0.15
  auto_rollback_if_error_rate_gt: 0.02
```

claire: Sounds good. Reminder: test on staging with simulated SNAT exhaustion and stickiness first.

alex: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the coordination channel. I'll post updates once SNAT patch completes. :thumbsup:
